name: The Great Ocean Road
tagline: A 243-kilometre coastal drive of surf beaches, rainforest and limestone stacks rising from the Southern Ocean, and one of the world's great road trips.
highlight: The Twelve Apostles at sunset, as the limestone stacks glow gold in the surf.
shortDescription: A war memorial road built by returned soldiers, winding past Bells Beach, Lorne, Apollo Bay, the Otway rainforest and the Twelve Apostles, with wildlife, waterfalls and shipwreck history.
metaDescription: A Great Ocean Road travel guide: the Twelve Apostles, Loch Ard Gorge, London Arch, Lorne, Apollo Bay, Otway National Park, koalas, when to go, how long to allow and a two-day itinerary from Melbourne.
nearestAirport: Melbourne Tullamarine (MEL), about 1.5–3 hours to the start
knownFor: The Twelve Apostles, coastal scenery, surf, rainforest, koalas
goodFor: Road trips, coastal scenery, walking, wildlife, photography

image.file: File:Princetown (AU), Port Campbell National Park, Twelve Apostles -- 2019 -- 0969.jpg
image.alt: The Twelve Apostles limestone stacks rising from the sea off the Victorian coast

intro: The Great Ocean Road runs for about 243 km along Victoria's south-west coast, from Torquay to Allansford. It was built between 1919 and 1932 by returned soldiers of the First World War, as a memorial to their fallen comrades, and it is often called the world's largest war memorial. The road hugs cliffs and beaches, and is a slow, winding drive that is as much about the stops as the destination.

The route passes surf beaches such as Bells Beach, seaside towns such as Lorne and Apollo Bay, the temperate Otway rainforest with waterfalls and tall trees, and finally the spectacular Shipwreck Coast, where limestone cliffs and stacks have been carved by the Southern Ocean. The best-known are the Twelve Apostles, though fewer than a dozen stacks now remain, and one collapsed in 2005.

Many visitors do it as a long day trip from Melbourne, which is tiring, and it is much better with a night or two on the road. Koalas in the trees at Kennett River, whales offshore in winter, and small fishing towns make it rewarding for those who take their time.

whyVisit.intro: It is one of the most scenic drives in the world, and easy to reach from Melbourne.

points.title: The Twelve Apostles
points.text: A group of limestone stacks in the sea, at their best at sunrise and sunset.

points.title: Dramatic coastline
points.text: Cliffs, gorges, arches and sea stacks along the Shipwreck Coast.

points.title: Rainforest and waterfalls
points.text: The Otway Ranges have giant trees, ferns and tumbling falls.

points.title: Wildlife
points.text: Wild koalas, kangaroos, and whales in the winter months.

points.title: Small seaside towns
points.text: Lorne, Apollo Bay and Port Fairy for seafood and a slower pace.

attractionsIntro: The route is best in stages, with stops for scenery and walks.

attractions.name: The Twelve Apostles
attractions.text: Limestone stacks standing off the cliff line near Port Campbell, best seen from the boardwalks and viewing platforms. Helicopter flights are available.
attractions.tip: Go at sunrise or late afternoon, when tour buses are fewer.

attractions.name: Loch Ard Gorge

image.alt: The sheltered beach and cliffs of Loch Ard Gorge on the Victorian coast

attractions.text: A gorge with a small beach and dramatic cliffs, named after a ship wrecked in 1878. Only two of the 54 people on board survived.

attractions.name: London Arch

image.file: File:London Arch on the Great Ocean Road (500895555).jpg
image.alt: The limestone arch known as London Arch on the Great Ocean Road

attractions.text: A natural limestone arch formerly known as London Bridge, whose span collapsed in 1990, stranding two visitors on the outer section, who were rescued by helicopter.
attractions.tip: See it on the same stop as the Grotto.

attractions.name: Lorne and the Otway Ranges

image.file: File:Great Ocean Road, Lorne, Australia - Feb 2012.jpg
image.alt: The Great Ocean Road curving along the coast near Lorne

attractions.text: Lorne is a popular beach town with waterfalls in the hinterland, including Erskine Falls, and the Otway rainforest inland, with the Otway Fly Treetop Walk.

attractions.name: Kennett River koalas
attractions.text: A short stretch of road where koalas are often seen in gum trees, along with colourful parrots.
attractions.tip: Look up, and do not feed the birds.

attractions.name: Bells Beach
attractions.text: One of the most famous surf breaks in the world, near Torquay, home of the Rip Curl Pro surfing competition.
attractions.tip: Visit the Australian National Surfing Museum in Torquay.

thingsToDoIntro: The road is the experience, with time for walks, wildlife and food.

thingsToDo.title: Drive the coast
thingsToDo.text: Take the route slowly, stopping at lookouts.
thingsToDo.tip: Allow twice as long as the drive time.

thingsToDo.title: Watch sunrise or sunset at the Apostles
thingsToDo.text: The stacks glow in the low light, and crowds are thinner.
thingsToDo.tip: Stay nearby to avoid driving in the dark.

thingsToDo.title: Walk in the Otway rainforest
thingsToDo.text: Short walks to waterfalls, or the treetop walk in the canopy.

thingsToDo.title: Look for koalas at Kennett River
thingsToDo.text: See wild koalas in eucalypts near the road.

thingsToDo.title: Try surfing at Torquay
thingsToDo.text: Lessons are available at the surf beaches.

thingsToDo.title: Whale-watch in winter
thingsToDo.text: Southern right whales come to Warrnambool from May to September.
thingsToDo.tip: Look from the Logans Beach viewing platform.

foodIntro: The Great Ocean Road has excellent seafood and local produce, and small-town cafés.

foods.name: Fresh seafood
foods.text: Crayfish, scallops, abalone and fish and chips at harbour-side cafés.

foods.name: Local dairy and cheese
foods.text: Cheese and milk from the nearby dairy farms.

foods.name: Cool-climate wine
foods.text: Pinot noir and chardonnay from the Otways and Geelong.

foods.name: Craft beer
foods.text: Small breweries in Apollo Bay and Torquay.

foods.name: Bakery pies
foods.text: Hearty meat pies from coastal bakeries.

accommodation.intro: Small towns along the route offer everything from motels to boutique stays.

areas.name: Lorne
areas.text: A lively seaside resort with many options.

areas.name: Port Campbell
areas.text: A small town near the main sights.

gettingThere.intro: The road starts about 100 km south-west of Melbourne.

options.text: About 1.5 hours to Torquay and about 4.5 hours to the Twelve Apostles without stops.
Day tours run from Melbourne, and multi-day tours are available.

options.mode: Train to Geelong and a car
options.text: Trains reach Geelong, and buses continue to the coast.

gettingAround.intro: A car is the best way, and the road is slow.

options.text: Winding, narrow roads with limited overtaking.
options.detail: Drive on the left, and take breaks.

options.text: Short walks at the main stops.

bestTime.headline: December–April
bestTime.summary: The south coast has a cool, changeable climate, with rain and wind in winter and pleasant summers.

seasons.text: Warm, dry and busy, with long days.
Cold, wet and stormy, but with whales and dramatic seas.

bestTime.avoid: Summer weekends and school holidays, when the road is busy.

itinerary.title: Two days on the Great Ocean Road
itinerary.intro: The first half on the first day, and the Shipwreck Coast on the second.

days.title: The Shipwreck Coast
days.morning: Kennett River koalas and the Otways.
days.afternoon: The Twelve Apostles and Loch Ard Gorge.

tipsIntro: A few tips make the drive better.
tips: Stay overnight rather than doing a day trip.
Drive slowly, and use pull-outs to let others pass.
Take breaks. Fatigue is a hazard on winding roads.
Visit the Apostles at sunrise or late afternoon.
Stay on the boardwalks and paths near cliffs.
Fill up with fuel in the larger towns.
Bring layers, since the coast is windy.

faq.q: How long does the Great Ocean Road take?
faq.a: The drive takes about 5 to 6 hours from Torquay to Allansford without stops. Allow two days.

faq.q: Can I do it as a day trip from Melbourne?
faq.a: Yes, but it is a long day of about 12 hours. It is better with a night on the way.
There were never twelve, and fewer than a dozen stacks remain. One collapsed in 2005.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: December to April for weather. Winter has whales but is wet.
It is best, but tours are available.

faq.q: Can I swim on the Great Ocean Road?
faq.a: At patrolled beaches such as Lorne, yes. Many beaches have strong currents and no lifeguards.
